senses.gloss:
Paila
(‘descendant of the sage Pila’)
------------------------------------------
The sage कृष्ण द्वैपायन has been credited with achieving the great task of collecting all the Vedic mantras extant during his time, editing them by dividing them into four books and teaching them to his four chief disciples. Hence he came to be known as वेदव्यास or व्यास (vyas = to divide, to edit). These four books—known as the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda and the Atharvaveda—were taught respectively to the sages पैल, वैशम्पायन, जैमिनि and सुमन्तु.
Thus पैल, a descendant of the ancient sage Pila, was the first disciple of वेदव्यास through whom the Ṛgveda was propagated. Nothing more is known about him.
